thread:
developer (AcmeDev): hey team — between 11:22–11:25 UTC a bunch of our streaming calls to /v1/streams showed up as 5xx in billing. client closed the tab, only got ~200 tokens each. charging looks like full 5xx. trace: trace-id=acme-zz-11

erin (support): sorry to hear that. can you paste a minimal repro (curl or SDK) and one request id from the period? we should be treating client-initiated closes as client aborts, not a gateway 5xx. :pray:

developer (AcmeDev): thanks — sample request below. using nodejs sdk v1.2.0, streaming with `response.on('data')` then client nav close. one request id: req=7f9b2b. server headers/snippet: 
```
> GET /v1/streams
> Transfer-Encoding: chunked
> Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
```
server side: `proxy -> upstream` shows `RST_STREAM` then `502` logged by gateway. attach small tcpdump showing FIN from client right after chunk 2.

alex (eng-oncall): looking. initial hypothesis: our gateway currently classifies certain mid-stream socket resets as upstream failures when chunked trailer isn't seen. if the client sends FIN/FIN_WAIT immediately after partial chunk, proxy can race and surface as 5xx. that matches `RST_STREAM` + 502. we have a heuristic for `halfclose` but it seems not catching this path. can you repro with curl? `curl -N -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" --data-binary @- https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams` and then ctrl-c after first chunk.

sam (infra): adding details — our proxy marks requests as 5xx when we observe upstream EOF before final chunk trailer *and* no `Connection: close` from client. some clients (mobile/webviews) do TCP FIN without trailer which we currently treat as upstream failure. i'll pull traces for req=7f9b2b. ops-bot created INC-2026 for investigation.

erin (support): thanks. i'm going to flag affected invoices and start a provisional refund for the accounts that hit >1 such event in that window. need eng confirmation before mass refunds.

alex (eng-oncall): plan: 1) add more conservative classification: if client FIN occurs within 1s of last chunk, treat as client-abort (no 5xx). 2) add extra logging for `RST_STREAM` vs `FIN` so we can split billing metrics. i'll open PR with test harness that injects FIN mid-chunk.

developer (AcmeDev): appreciated. rough ETA? customers noticed a small billing spike.

alex (eng-oncall): i'll aim for a patch and deploy to canary in a few hours, then roll to prod with metrics. if the canary looks good we'll flip billing classification.

erin (support): i'll pause refunds until you confirm canary result, but I'll mark the invoices as disputed in billing so no auto-charge.

sam (infra): quick runnable repro snippet i used to simulate: 
```
# python partial_chunk.py
import socket, time
s=socket.create_connection(('api.redwood.ai',443))
# handshake omitted for brevity
s.send(b"POST /v1/streams HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: api.redwood.ai\r\nTransfer-Encoding: chunked\r\nAuthorization: Bearer x\r\n\r\n3\r\nhey\r\n")
# close socket immediately
s.close()
```
this reproduces 502 in our current proxy config.

ops-bot: incident INC-2026 created (severity: low, owners: @alex, @sam).

alex (eng-oncall): thanks all — will post updates in this thread after canary. for now workaround for clients: send an explicit final zero-length chunk `0\r\n\r\n` before closing or set `Connection: close` header when closing early.

erin (support): noted, i'll pass workaround to Acme and add to public docs 

developer (AcmeDev): will try the workaround and report back. thanks! :thumbsup:
